original:
# Pump P-200, line 3

Pump P-200 on line 3 was inspected on Monday after the operators reported water under the housing. The shaft seal is worn and lets about twenty drops a minute through, which is well above what the manufacturer allows.

The technician will replace the seal MS-40 on Thursday morning. The work takes about two hours, and line 3 runs on the standby pump in that time. The visit and the seal are covered by the service contract.

The worn seal goes to the manufacturer for analysis, so that the next inspection can look for the same wear before it leads to a leak. Until Thursday, the operators check the drip tray at the start of every shift and note how much water it holds.

If the leak gets worse before the visit, switch the pump off, change over to the standby pump and call the service desk on the number in the contract.

Please let us know if Thursday does not suit you. We can arrange another visit within the week. Thank you for reporting the leak so quickly.
